cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: When you type a URL and press Enter, the request passes a chain of systems, each with one job, before anything renders: DNS, TCP and TLS, the HTTP request, CDN, load balancer, security gate, API gateway, auth, cache and database, queue, response, render.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: A CDN edge serves cached assets and ends the journey early; only cache misses reach the origin. Behind it: load balancer, rate limiting and WAF, API gateway, then the service checks session or JWT, reads cache then database, pushes slow work to a queue, and returns the response for the browser to render.

questions.q: Does every page load go through all these steps?
questions.a: No. DNS is cached, keep-alive and HTTP/2 reuse connections, and CDN hits skip the origin. Skipping steps is where performance comes from.

questions.q: What are the three TCP handshake messages?

questions.a: Onto a queue for async workers, so the response returns quickly.
